extracted.intended_audience: KIPO patent examiners and patent office staff (also relevant to applicants and their representatives)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures, classification criteria, confidentiality handling, storage, publication, appeals, and overseas-filing permissions for patent applications related to national defense under the Korean Patent Act and KIPO directives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision content for registration/ rejection of term extension
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining whether to register an extension of the patent term due to delay in registration, the examiner shall write a decision to register extension or a decision to reject registration for extension indicating the followings and sign and seal such decision. However, a decision to reject registration for extension shall not contain the items ③ and ④ below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required items to include in the decision: ① Application Number of Registration of Extension; ② Patent Number; ③ Period for Extension; ④ Content of Period of Delay; ⑤ Name and Address of Applicant (Title and Business Address for a legal entity); ⑥ If a representative is present, Name and Address or Business Address of Representative (Title, Business Address and Name of Designated Patent Attorney where representative is a patent law firm); ⑦ Order and Ground for Decision; ⑧ Date of Decision. (Note: rejection decisions omit items ③ and ④.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of decision on extension registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Where registration for extension of the term of a patent right due to a delay in registration is determined, the Commissioner of the Korean Intellectual Property Office shall serve a certified copy of the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details related to transmittal of a decision shall follow the provisions regarding transmittal of a certified copy of a decision to grant/reject a patent right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Gazette publication for registered extension
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examiner determines registration of extension of the patent term due to a delay in registration, the Registration Division shall publish specified items on the patent gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items to publish: ① name and address of patent right holder (title and business address for a legal entity); ② patent number; ③ date of registration for extension; ④ period for extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal period for rejection of extension registration
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who received a decision to reject patent term extension may appeal the decision by submitting a notice of appeal trial to the decision to reject registration for extension within thirty days from the date of transmittal of a certified copy of the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict 30-day deadline measured from transmittal date of certified copy; appeal is via notice of appeal trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation trial for patent rights registered for extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent right whose term is extended falls under any paragraph of Article 134-2 of the Patent Act since the application to register patent term extension due to a delay in registration is determined for registration of extension, an applicant can request a trial to invalidate the patent right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If statutory grounds for invalidation (Article 134-2) apply to an extended patent right, a party may petition for invalidation trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government powers over national-defense inventions (Article 41)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government may prohibit filing a patent application with a foreign patent office or may order an inventor, applicant, or agent to keep confidential an invention for which a patent application has been filed, if necessary for national defense; may refuse to grant a patent; may expropriate patent entitlement during war/incidents/emergencies; and shall pay reasonable compensation for losses incurred by prohibition/refusal/expropriation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences of violating an order: person shall be deemed to relinquish entitlement to a patent and to claims for compensation. Procedures for prohibiting filing overseas, classifying as confidential, expropriation and compensation are prescribed by Presidential Decree.

rubrics_metrics.name: KIPO determination of classification criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner of the Korean Intellectual Property Office shall determine the classification criteria necessary for selection of inventions to be treated as confidential under Article 41(1) after consulting with the Commissioner of the Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification criteria are set by KIPO directive (e.g., Directive No.651 / No.822) after consultation with DAPA and are used to identify national defense-related IPC/CPC codes and other selection features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral procedure for confidential treatment (Enforcement Decree Article 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent application filed by a person domiciled or having business in Korea conforms to the classification criteria, the Commissioner of KIPO shall refer the application to the Commissioner of DAPA to determine whether it should be classified and treated as confidential, and shall notify the inventor/applicant/agent and request them to maintain confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referral to DAPA initiates confidential-handling process; the applicant and related persons are formally requested to observe confidentiality pending DAPA reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: DAPA response timeframe and KIPO action
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner of DAPA shall reply within two months upon receiving a reference; if it deems confidentiality necessary, it shall request KIPO to classify and treat the application as confidential. Upon receiving such a request, KIPO shall take necessary measures under confidential service rules and order inventor/applicant to maintain confidentiality; if not requested, KIPO shall notify cancellation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-month consultation window with DAPA; KIPO acts promptly on DAPA requests to classify or to cancel confidentiality requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic review of confidentiality status
rubrics_metrics.description: For patent applications ordered to be confidential, the Commissioner of KIPO shall take necessary measures after consulting twice or more each year with the Commissioner of DAPA on cancellation of confidentiality, extension of confidential maintenance period, or change of confidentiality level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least biannual consultation to reassess ongoing need for confidentiality and adjust level or duration accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant rights to request release or change of confidential treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: An inventor/applicant/agent ordered to classify and treat a patent application as confidential may request KIPO to release it from confidential treatment, to change the confidential level, or to publish or license the invention within specified limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal request procedures exist for applicants to seek lifting or modification of confidentiality constraints; KIPO considers such requests in consultation with DAPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of national defense-related application classifications
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two types: (1) applications filed with the applicant's indication of national defense-related application (handled by secret retention and referral to DAPA), and (2) applications classified by KIPO (IPC/CPC code) as national defense-related, including certain international applications listed in Directive No.822.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant-indicated cases: submitted in writing, kept secret, transferred for classification. International/PCT cases: transmittal to IB/ISA may be withheld and docs transferred to competent examination division when matching classification standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application types eligible for national-defense classification
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application and a utility model application (mutatis mutandis) are eligible to be classified as national defense-related; international applications under the PCT may also be withheld/transferred if they fall under the classification standard (PCT Article 27(8)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility model and PCT international filings are covered by analogous provisions; treatment per applicable rules (withholding transmittal to IB/ISA and transferring to examination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of written handling and online filing exception
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, national defense-related applications shall take proceedings in writing. However, where an applicant is unaware that his/her application is crucial to national defense, the applicant can file online; an examiner can then classify and specially manage the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most national defense-related applications are submitted in writing (e.g., by defense institutes) with an indication; online filings may be converted to confidential handling if later recognized as national defense-related.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling when applicant files with indication of national defense
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant files a national defense-related application in writing, the receiving division shall keep the application secret, transmit a copy to DAPA to check confidentiality necessity, and request inventor/applicant/representative to keep the application secret. If confidentiality is requested, only bibliographic data is entered electronically and the application is transferred to Patent Examination Policy Division for classification and then to the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If consultation determines confidentiality is not needed, lift confidentiality order and proceed with normal written handling, and notify inventor/applicant/representative of lifting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling where applicant notifies national defense after electronic filing but before transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant electronically filed without indicating national defense but notifies before transfer to examination division, the Application Service Division director shall ask Information Management to print documents confidentially and delete the electronic documents on PatentNet; printed handling rules for indicated filings then apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires confidential printing of original, copy, and storage media (e.g., floppy disc), deletion of electronic files to avoid public exposure, and application of the standard confidential handling procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner review when CPC/IPC code matches national defense list
rubrics_metrics.description: When assigning classification code under CPC/IPC and the section/class matches codes determined as national defense-related, the examiner shall determine whether to treat the application as national defense-related. Normally such applications need to be treated as national defense-related unless grounds for exception exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KIPI/KIPO coding by Korea Institute of Patent Information may notify examiner. Examiner must consider exceptions per Directive No.822(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to national-defense treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may not be treated as national defense-related where: applicant lacks domicile/business in Korea; it does not fall under major defense materials or specified weapons systems; or the examiner recognizes it can be kept secret for national defense (i.e., not requiring special treatment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also consider prior public disclosure, lack of relation to national security/military secrets, or initial misclassification where the application was laid open to the public before change — these are grounds to avoid confidential treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation when uncertain about national-defense classification
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is hard to determine whether to handle the application as national defense-related, an examiner may consult with the Director of the Emergency Affairs Subsection from the General Services Division, an applicant, or a military expert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use internal/external expertise to resolve borderline classification cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when examiner changes classification during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If during examination a classified application should be designated national defense-related and has no ground for exemption, the examiner shall change the IPC code to the national defense code and initiate confidentiality procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report and follow the Annexed Form 31 of Administrative Instructions of Security Operational Rule, and proceed with printing/deletion/transfer steps described for confidential cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality consultation and printing/deletion workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application reported by an examiner is recognized as legitimate for national defense classification, the Patent Examination Policy Division director shall request printing of the electronic files, delete the electronic file (except bibliographic items and history), and transfer the original and copies confidentially; the copy is sent to DAPA to confirm need for confidentiality and inventor/applicant/rep are requested to observe confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information Management prints original, copy, and a copy of storage media, transfers them confidentially, and deletes the electronic file from PatentNet. If confidentiality is not required, the director lifts the confidentiality order and asks to shift the application back to electronic file for ordinary examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedure for confidential applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedure for examining a confidential application is the same as for an ordinary application, but the examiner must be extra cautious about maintaining confidentiality when borrowing confidential documents from the examination bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner determines to grant a patent on a confidential application, final documents including amendments and written arguments are sent to Patent Examination Policy Division; if rejecting, final documents sent to Information Management Division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management rules for confidential application documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Divisions managing confidential documents or examiners shall carefully maintain confidentiality according to prescribed measures, including regular consultation with DAPA and procedural requirements on notification, storage, and handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific measures: notify grant/registration in writing to Registration Service and Information Management Division; withhold confidential applications from laying-open/publication until confidentiality order is lifted; if confidentiality lifted, lay open/publish without delay; registration documents kept by Patent Examination Policy Division until confidentiality lifted; assign management numbers to rejected confidential applications and handle under confidential-doc rules; amendments and written arguments shall not be assigned management numbers but filed together in original and copy; copies kept with management number apart from original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure storage and access controls for confidential files
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential applications must not be stored with ordinary patent applications and shall be kept in a double-layered steel container with the director of the Patent Examination Policy Division primarily responsible for management; confidentiality register and management numbers must be recorded for identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidential files of patent registrations and rejections can be lent only by writing on the confidential check-out list; the rules specify authorized person controls (note: guidance text indicates restrictions on check-out). Further details refer to Administrative Instructions of the Security Operational Rule (Article 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on filing overseas for national-defense inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Article 41, an invention crucial for national defense can be banned from filing overseas and can be filed abroad only with government permission. Filing abroad in violation is deemed abandonment of right to a patent and may incur liability to pay reasonable compensation for losses due to violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications banned from overseas filing are those classified by KIPO as confidential or indicated by applicant as national defense-related, and those deemed necessary to be kept confidential after consultation with DAPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission to file overseas (conditions and procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Korean government grants permission to file a patent application banned from filing overseas, an application may exceptionally file abroad subject to conditions. Korea has an agreement with the United States permitting filing in the US under confidentiality agreements; otherwise filing abroad is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain permission to file in the United States, applicant must submit a written request (Annex Form No.21). Conditions for permission include: 1) the specification must be clear and specific to examine the application in the US; 2) the right to claim damages caused by confidentiality in the US shall be waived (except for damages from US use/disclosure without permission). After filing in the US with permission, applicant must: attach two copies of application documents; attach copy of KIPO-issued permission; attach copy of representative's personal info and US security clearance documents; submit these to DAPA; designate a representative who has received US government security clearance; and immediately notify DAPA of the US application number and filing date.
